exposure: loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) for CIN 2-3
outcome: treatment failure (recurrence or residual disease of CIN)
preterm-related complications (short cervix, preterm labor, preterm premature rupture of the membrane)
cohort: The study included 385 patients who underwent loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grades 2-3 between 2011 and 2019, with 31 patients subsequently delivering after LEEP.
finding: Positive HPV status after LEEP and positive surgical margins were identified as independent risk factors for treatment failure (recurrence or residual disease) in patients with CIN who underwent LEEP.
